# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working on an MPShips app. This project was generated from the MPShips cookiecutter template and is built on the `MPShipsApp` base class from `mpships_infra`.

## The one rule that matters most

**Do not modify the app structure.** The project layout, entry points, and class skeleton generated by the template are what the MPShips platform loads. Changing them breaks registration, routing, or deployment, often without an obvious error locally.

Do not:

- rename, move, or delete files or folders that the template generated
- edit `run_app.py` or the code that calls `create_app()`
- rename the app class (its name is shown in the navigation menu and used to look up app metadata)
- change the `mpships_infra` imports or the `MPShipsApp` base class
- add new top-level packages, entry points, or configuration files

If a task seems to require a structural change, stop and ask the human instead of making it.

## What you may modify

Only the three hooks on the app class:

| Hook | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ships_setup(self)` | No | One-time setup. Set read-only instance state (`self.my_value = ...`). |
| `ships_layout(self)` | **Yes** | Return the Dash layout. |
| `ships_callbacks(self, app, cache)` | No | Register callbacks with `@app.callback`. |

- Imports at the top of the file are fine.
- Keep app logic inside the three hooks. If you need a helper, define it as a nested function inside a hook.
- Do not override `__init__`, `get_layout`, or `generate_callbacks`. The framework calls the hooks for you.
- Do not call `super()` in any hook. None is needed.
- Do not assign to these reserved read-only properties: `name`, `description`, `long_description`, `url`, `author`, `category`, `credits`, `icon`, `dois`, `docs_url`, `external_links`, `contributed`, `contributed_app`. Use a different attribute name instead, such as `self.display_label`.

## Callbacks

- Register callbacks inside `ships_callbacks` with `@app.callback`. Do not use module-level `@callback`.
- Treat values set in `ships_setup` as read-only. Do not assign to `self` attributes inside a callback, because one running app serves many users and that state would be shared.
- Keep per-user state in `dcc.Store`, or pass it through callback inputs and outputs.

## Paths and assets

Assets (CSS, JS, images) may be added to the existing `assets/` folder. Dash loads CSS and JS from it automatically.

Never hardcode absolute paths. The app is served from a different base path when deployed.

```python
import dash

# Wrong
html.Img(src="/assets/logo.png")
html.A("Results", href="/results")

# Right
html.Img(src=dash.get_asset_url("logo.png"))
html.A("Results", href=dash.get_relative_path("/results"))
```

- Call these inside the hooks, not at import time.
- Wrap a `dcc.Location` pathname with `dash.strip_relative_path(pathname)` before comparing it.
- Use full URLs (`https://...`) for external resources.

## Dependencies

- Add any new dependency to `pyproject.toml`, pinned to an exact version (`package==1.2.3`).
- Install it in the project's virtual environment so it can be tested.
- Do not add `requirements.txt`, `setup.py`, or other dependency files.

## Data

- Fetch Materials Project data with `get_rester()` from `mpships_infra`. Do not create your own `MPRester`.
- It reads the API key from the `MP_API_KEY` environment variable. Never hardcode or commit a key.

## Other constraints

- Do not commit large files (datasets, model weights, videos, compiled binaries).
- Keep any text, labels, and styles in the layout. Use Bulma classes (`title`, `subtitle`, `content`, and so on), because the Bulma stylesheet is loaded by default.

## Before finishing

1. Run `python run_app.py` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8050/`.
2. Confirm the page renders and every callback responds without errors in the terminal.
3. Check that the diff only touches the three hooks, the imports, `assets/`, and `pyproject.toml`.
